cells.tense: Right now you're steering by what actually moves you, and the steering is steady.
cells.ask: Offer the next piece of the dream out loud — say what you'd build if the resources were already there — and let the saying show you which part is real.
cells.core:
You're in a stretch where effort has stopped feeling like effort. What you want and what you care about are pointed the same way, so the work carries itself and you keep adjusting as you go without it costing you anything. That's not luck. That's you reading the situation well enough to stop forcing it.

So there's room now for something bigger than the next step — a picture of what all this could add up to, said out loud where you can hear it. Say it while it's still forming and see which part holds when it hits the air.
cells.sheetLine: Effort feels natural right now, and you're the one steering.
cells.verb: finding the pace where what you want and what you feel move together

cells.tense: You're running the next few moves ahead of where you actually are, and the tension is in the gap.
cells.ask: Pull one scattered thing back into the same picture as the rest — write the loose pieces down next to each other until they line up — and then take the next step from what lines up rather than from the worry.
cells.core:
There's a version of how this should go that you keep trying to hold in place, and holding it is taking more than the doing would. You're bracing for the turn before the road gets there, checking the plan against a future that keeps changing shape — and the grip itself is what's making the movement uneven. The push has gotten ahead of the thing it was pushing.

Gather the loose pieces instead. When a few things that feel like separate worries get set side by side, they usually turn out to be one problem with one next move — and that move is calmer than the bracing was.
cells.sheetLine: You're forcing a rhythm that hasn't arrived yet.

cells.tense: You've been waiting at a gate that already swung open, still treating the before as the now.
cells.ask: Gather what actually came of the last big change — count the real yield, small as it is — and let that accounting tell you which direction has energy in it before you commit to anything new.
cells.core:
Adjusting the blend takes something to blend, and you've been low on that — the wants feel far away, the nudge toward moving isn't there, and days pass without anything being steered. Not because you can't feel. Because the tank you'd steer from is empty, and pushing feeling and effort into it directly just makes the emptiness louder.

More effort in the same spot won't fill it. Looking at what the last real change actually produced will — what you kept, what grew, what it taught — and letting that accounting give the empty gauge something to read. What was already grown gets gathered; the direction comes back from there.
cells.sheetLine: The direction's gone quiet and pushing at it isn't bringing it back.

cells.tense: You're already adjusting and steering every day — you just talk about it as if the situation were doing the steering.
cells.ask: Pick one small thing you keep adjusting and do it on purpose — deliberately, once, all the way through — and notice that the adjusting was always yours.
cells.core:
You are the one finding the balance in this. You read the room, you shift the blend, you make the small calls that keep things flowing — and then you describe it as just how things are, or as the work requiring it, or as keeping the peace. The steering is happening. The owning of it isn't.

Start smaller than feels reasonable. One adjustment you already make, done deliberately and finished on purpose, is enough to show you who's been at the wheel — and that showing is what turns the craft from something that happens to you into something you build.
cells.sheetLine: You're already steering this. You've been calling it the situation.
